items.title: 2.8 Electronic configuration and the periodic table

source_refs.note: Topic 2.8, printed page 38: configuration from position in the table (Figure 2.15, carried by the chapter 1 periodic table original).

blocks.text: The electronic configurations of the elements are related to their position in the periodic table, which is structured so that elements with the same pattern of outer-shell (valence) electron configuration fall in the same groups. An element's configuration can therefore be written from its location in the table, and the elements can be grouped by the type of orbital into which their electrons are placed.

items: On the left are two columns, the alkali metals and alkaline earth metals of groups 1 and 2, in which the outer-shell s orbitals are being filled; group 1 and 2 elements have ns1 and ns2 outer configurations respectively. Jumping to group 13, the configuration is ns2 np1.
On the right is a block of six columns in which the outermost p orbitals are being filled.
In the middle is a block of ten columns containing the transition metals, in which the d orbitals are being filled.
Below the main table are two rows of fourteen columns, the f block elements, in which the f orbitals are being filled.

blocks.text: The numbers 2, 6, 10 and 14 are precisely the numbers of electrons that can fill the s, p, d and f subshells.

blocks.alt: A schematic periodic table of seven period rows and eighteen group columns. The s block is pink at the left, the d block blue in the middle, the p block cream at the right, and the two f block rows purple below; a thick black stair-step line runs from boron down to polonium, and symbols mark the edges of each block.
blocks.caption: The blocks of the periodic table follow the subshell being filled (the chapter 1 original, after Figures 1.1 and 10.2; also the frame of Figures 2.15 and 2.16).
blocks.long_description: The two columns of the s block (groups 1 and 2) fill the ns subshell with 2 electrons, the six columns of the p block (groups 13 to 18) fill np with 6, the ten columns of the d block fill (n - 1)d with 10, and the fourteen columns of the f block below fill (n - 2)f with 14. Reading across the periods gives the building-up order: 1s; 2s then 2p; 3s then 3p; 4s, 3d then 4p.

blocks.prompt: Using the periodic table, write the configuration of cadmium (Z = 48) and lanthanum (Z = 57) as a noble-gas core plus the electrons beyond it, and the full configuration of antimony (Z = 51) with its number of unpaired electrons.
blocks.explanation: Cadmium ends period 5's d block: [Kr] 4d10 5s2. Lanthanum begins the lanthanides after the 6s pair: [Xe] 5d1 6s2 (the first f block position). Antimony, group 15 of period 5, is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10 4s2 4p6 4d10 5s2 5p3; its three 5p electrons are unpaired, so three.

items: Position in the table gives the configuration: groups 1 and 2 fill ns (ns1, ns2), groups 13 to 18 fill np (from ns2 np1), the ten middle columns fill d, the fourteen columns below fill f; 2, 6, 10 and 14 are the subshell capacities.
